group.name: Cisco Nexus Switch Receiver
group.description: Dashboard group for SSH/NX-OS switch metrics emitted by the Cisco OS receiver, focused on Nexus reachability, interfaces, VXLAN/EVPN fabric state, vPC/LACP, optics, and hardware health.

dashboards.name: 00 Nexus Switch Telemetry And Device Health
dashboards.description: Value: first-response dashboard for Nexus SSH collection trust, device reachability, system pressure, and control-plane CPU evidence.
dashboards.value: Use this page before deeper switch triage. It separates collector or device reachability problems from CPU, memory, uptime, and control-plane process pressure.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to use the Nexus switch health dashboard. Interpretation: start with reachability and partial scrape state, then use CPU, memory, uptime, and process CPU to decide whether the device or collection path is the first failure domain.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
Use this page first for Nexus switch incidents collected over SSH. It proves whether telemetry is trustworthy and whether the switch itself is busy before operators investigate interfaces, fabric control plane, redundancy, optics, or hardware.

charts.name: Device Reachability
charts.description: Value: identifies Nexus switches that stopped responding to SSH collection. Interpretation: 1 means reachable, 0 means unreachable.

charts.name: Partial Scrapes
charts.description: Value: shows whether one or more NX-OS command families failed. Interpretation: 1 means the scrape was incomplete and adjacent charts may be missing evidence.

charts.name: System CPU And Memory
charts.description: Value: shows device-wide CPU and memory pressure. Interpretation: sustained high utilization means interface or control-plane symptoms may be secondary to system pressure.

charts.name: Device Uptime
charts.description: Value: shows recent reload or uptime reset evidence. Interpretation: sudden drops indicate reboot, switchover, or collection reset context for the incident window.

charts.name: Control Plane Process CPU
charts.description: Value: identifies which control-plane process family is driving CPU. Interpretation: spikes by process point the operator toward routing, management, telemetry, or platform process ownership.

dashboards.name: 01 Nexus Interfaces L2 And QoS Congestion
dashboards.description: Value: interface, packet, QoS, and L2 troubleshooting dashboard for congestion, drops, storms, and policy pressure.
dashboards.value: Use this page when users report slow or lossy service through a Nexus switch. It connects interface utilization, packet mix, drops/errors, QoS queues, policy counters, and L2 churn.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to use interface, L2, and QoS evidence. Interpretation: correlate utilization and packet volume with drops/errors, QoS class or queue bytes, and STP/LACP symptoms to identify the likely owner.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page focuses on user-impacting link and queue symptoms. It correlates interface traffic, utilization, packet volume, drops, errors, QoS queue bytes, policy bytes, and L2 state so NetOps can separate congestion from physical or topology instability.

charts.name: Interface Traffic Rate
charts.description: Value: shows RX/TX bandwidth pressure by switch interface. Interpretation: sustained increases, silence, or asymmetry point to path changes or congestion.

charts.name: Interface Utilization
charts.description: Value: normalizes interface traffic by line speed. Interpretation: values near 1 indicate saturation risk.

charts.name: Packet Volume By Type
charts.description: Value: shows unicast, multicast, and broadcast packet volume by direction. Interpretation: unexpected multicast/broadcast growth can indicate storms, discovery loops, or workload shifts.

charts.name: Interface Errors And Drops
charts.description: Value: correlates packet errors and drops by interface. Interpretation: non-zero errors suggest physical or negotiation trouble; drops without errors point toward congestion, buffering, or QoS policy.

charts.name: QoS Queue Bytes
charts.description: Value: shows byte volume handled by queue or QoS group. Interpretation: high or shifting queue volume identifies the class most affected during congestion.

charts.name: QoS Policy Bytes
charts.description: Value: shows class-based policy byte volume by action and direction. Interpretation: drops, marks, or class shifts explain why specific traffic classes are slowed or discarded.

charts.name: LACP Errors
charts.description: Value: highlights link aggregation control-plane errors. Interpretation: spikes by interface explain member link removal or bundle instability.

charts.name: STP Instances And Changes
charts.description: Value: shows spanning-tree instance state and topology-change churn. Interpretation: unexpected blocked state or repeated topology changes indicate loop prevention or unstable L2 links.

dashboards.name: 02 Nexus VXLAN EVPN vPC And Redundancy
dashboards.description: Value: fabric control-plane and redundant-path dashboard for VXLAN, EVPN, vPC, port-channel, and neighbor evidence.
dashboards.value: Use this page when affected traffic depends on VXLAN/EVPN overlays or redundant access/fabric links. It surfaces peer, VNI, route, vPC, port-channel, and topology-neighbor health.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to use fabric and redundancy evidence. Interpretation: unhealthy peer, VNI, vPC, or port-channel rows identify the local failure domain before drilling into interfaces.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page separates overlay control-plane loss from redundant-path failures. NVE, VNI, EVPN route, vPC, port-channel, and topology-neighbor panels help NetOps identify whether the issue belongs to the fabric, peer, bundle, or local switch.

charts.name: VXLAN NVE Peer Status
charts.description: Value: finds failed VXLAN NVE peers. Interpretation: rows below healthy state identify underlay, BGP EVPN, or VTEP reachability issues.

charts.name: VXLAN VNI Status
charts.description: Value: finds VNI or segment-level VXLAN failures. Interpretation: unhealthy VNI rows point to tenant or segment control-plane issues even when NVE peers appear healthy.

charts.name: EVPN Route Inventory
charts.description: Value: shows EVPN route presence by VNI and route type. Interpretation: sudden drops indicate control-plane withdrawal or collection gaps.

charts.name: vPC Status
charts.description: Value: identifies vPC domain or peer-link problems. Interpretation: unhealthy rows explain dual-homed workload or fabric edge symptoms.

charts.name: vPC Consistency Failures
charts.description: Value: identifies vPC consistency failures by check. Interpretation: non-zero failures explain dual-homed host outages or blackholing risk.

charts.name: Port Channel Status
charts.description: Value: shows port-channel and member link health. Interpretation: down bundles or member loss indicates reduced capacity or broken redundant paths.

charts.name: Topology Neighbors
charts.description: Value: confirms expected LLDP/CDP neighbor visibility. Interpretation: missing or unexpected neighbor rows indicate cabling, peer, or discovery problems.

dashboards.name: 03 Nexus Hardware Optics And Capacity
dashboards.description: Value: physical health dashboard for hardware status, temperature, optics, and environmental symptoms.
dashboards.value: Use this page when interface symptoms may be caused by optics, cabling, fans, power supplies, modules, or thermal conditions.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to use hardware and optics evidence. Interpretation: correlate unhealthy component rows or drifting optical power with interface errors, drops, and user-impact windows.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
This page keeps physical evidence close to network symptoms. Optics, temperature, module, fan, PSU, and platform health explain CRCs, flaps, unexpected reloads, or degraded device capacity.

charts.name: Transceiver Sensors
charts.description: Value: tracks optical power, temperature, voltage, and laser bias. Interpretation: drift or threshold-adjacent values explain CRCs, link flaps, and optical path trouble.

charts.name: Hardware Status
charts.description: Value: surfaces fan, power, module, platform, and temperature health. Interpretation: unhealthy rows explain device instability or environmental risk.

charts.name: Hardware Temperature
charts.description: Value: tracks chassis, module, sensor, or platform temperature where exposed. Interpretation: rising or threshold-adjacent temperature explains throttling, fan alarms, or unstable hardware.

charts.name: Interface Traffic Rate
charts.description: Value: shows RX/TX bandwidth pressure by switch interface. Interpretation: sustained increases, silence, or asymmetry point to path changes or congestion.

charts.name: Interface Errors And Drops
charts.description: Value: gives physical triage immediate packet-loss context. Interpretation: errors rising with optical or temperature drift point toward physical path or hardware ownership.
